newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina poll shows little support for stadium.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina poll shows little support for stadium.

text.p: A poll of voters in North Carolina's 12-county Triad region found little support for public funding of a new baseball stadium, the Greensboro News & Record reported.
While the opinion poll found 60.8 percent of respondents favor a major league baseball stadium, only 35.4 percent said they would support a one-year, one-cent sales tax increase to pay for it.
The newspaper's Piedmont Opinion Survey division conducted the telephone poll of 523 randomly selected registered voters between April 24 and May 5. The error margin was 4.4 percent.

A bill authorizing tax increase referendums in the 12 counties is pending in the General Assembly. But some lawmakers in the district have said they would urge local officials not to put the proposal on the ballot in their counties.

It would create the Triad Metropolitan Baseball Park Authority to issue bonds for the $220 million stadium. The tax would only be levied if the region wins one of the two expansion teams scheduled to be awarded by 2000.
Counties in the proposed district are Alamance, Caswell, Davie, Davidson, Forsyth, Guilford, Montgomery, Randolph, Rockingham, Stokes, Surry and Yadkin.
